blocks.x: October has officially arrived in New York City, bringing crisp mornings, peak fall vibes, and a very good excuse to make dinner plans.

Between Halloween season taking over the city and fall foliage beginning to transform NYC’s parks, there’s plenty happening outside—but the city’s restaurant scene is giving us just as many reasons to stay out late.
A fresh slew of bars, restaurants, and buzzy new openings are popping up across the five boroughs, giving New Yorkers even more spots to add to their rotation.
From new neighborhood gems to splashy openings already making waves, these are the places you’ll want to know about this month.
Here are the new NYC bars and restaurants defining October.
iara – Now Open
Source / Ben Hon
205 Allen Street
iara, a new Brazilian open-kitchen restaurant inspired by the Amazon Rainforest, is now open in Long Island City, marking chef-owner Vitor Mendes’ first solo restaurant project.

The menu spotlights ingredients native to the Brazilian Amazon, including açaí, cassava, jambu, and tucupi, with dishes like tapioca and tuna, Rainforest Soup, pão de queijo, and charcoal-grilled seasonal greens.
Larger plates include Brazilian moqueca with red snapper, coconut milk, and tucupi and a 10-ounce charcoal-grilled picanha served with cassava fries, açaí ketchup, and toasted cassava flour.
Caputo Bagels – Now Open
Source / Max Flatow
81 Fifth Avenue
Caputo Bagels has officially opened in Park Slope, bringing a new generation of Caputo’s baking to the neighborhood in the form of hand-rolled sourdough bagels.

Made over roughly two days with a 45-year-old sourdough starter, the bagels are individually rolled, boiled, and baked in small batches throughout the day. The menu includes classics like Plain, Sesame, and Everything, plus cream cheeses, smoked salmon, whitefish, breakfast sandwiches, pastries, and coffee.
Don’t miss the Lard Provolone Bagel, a $4 nod to Caputo’s famous lard bread made with lard, meat, provolone, salt, and pepper.
Calabash – Opens Early October
Source / Rashida Zagon
183 Christopher Street

Calabash, a new Afro-Caribbean brasserie and bakery, is opening this October in the West Village, bringing together flavors and culinary traditions from West Africa, the Caribbean, and the Eastern Seaboard.

The 30-seat spot will serve everything from naturally fermented breads and laminated pastries in the morning to brasserie-style lunch and brunch dishes like suya steak & maduros and cornbread pancakes. Dinner will feature a five-course prix-fixe menu with dishes like Hoppin’ John dolma, red snapper with sweet corn and étouffée-style gravy, and crispy pork belly with tahdig jollof.
Calabash will also offer house-fermented mocktails, non-alcoholic wines, and adaptogenic drinks, plus a monthly Pay What You Can dinner.
Good Company – Opens October 8

Good Company, a new restaurant and cocktail bar from the team behind Yesterday’s, is opening October 8 in SoHo, bringing seasonal American fare, creative cocktails, and a warm, design-forward setting to New Yorkers.

The bi-level spot will serve shareable bites and comfort-food favorites like Wagyu French Dip Sliders, Grilled Mortadella Skewers, a signature Good Burger, Chicken Schnitty, and crispy fish sandwiches, alongside cocktails ranging from classics to inventive creations like the Matchapeno and Purple Negroni.
With its cozy interiors, greenery, and late-night vibe, Good Company is designed for everything from after-work drinks and date nights to dinner with friends.
